headline: Brazil Scrape Past Japan as Killer Instinct Finally Arrives
story: Japan's game plan of compact defending and rapid counters nearly yielded a startling upset. An early goal at 29' caught Brazil unprepared. Yet the pattern quickly reasserted itself: Brazil's possession and press smothered the contest. With 62% of the ball and 6.5 high-press phases to Japan's 2.1, the home side ground down their opponent across the middle two thirds. Brazil's build-up play recovered the ball every 16.9 seconds; Japan laboured at 26. The shape of the match was Brazilian control waiting for clinical finishing.

The numbers explained the 2-1 scoreline: Brazil's expected goals of 2.12 against Japan's 0.26 reflected a chasm in chance creation. Yet Brazil nearly paid the price for profligacy. At 54' a clear-cut opportunity went begging (xG 0.32, blocked); at 58' another dissolved under pressure (xG 0.31, saved). Gabriel Magalhaes and Bruno Guimarães imposed order at centre-back and midfield throughout. Late in added time, a final thrust breached Japan's exhausted shape for the winner. Control with a fortune clause attached.

keyMoment.text: Brazil's added-time breakthrough proved decisive after two gilt-edged chances went begging.

home.verdict: Dominated but danced with catastrophe; conversion finally came.
points: High-press intensity (6.5 phases vs 2.1) won control of midfield battle
Ball recovery time of 16.9s vs Japan's 26s dictated tempo throughout
Two big chances at 54' and 58' (xG 0.32, 0.31) nearly proved fatal

away.verdict: Gutsy early lead squandered by unequal pressing and recovery metrics.
points: Only 2.1 high-press phases vs Brazil's 6.5 left the midfield overrun
Ball recovery time of 26.0 seconds conceded possession dominance unchecked
Created just 0.26 xG—rare chances must be converted (not 0.12 gifts)

statLine: Brazil created 2.12 expected goals to Japan's 0.26, a gap reflecting utter dominance, yet required added time to overcome squandered precision.
